methods.name: eth_estimateGas
methods.description:
Generates and returns an estimate of how much gas is necessary to allow the transaction to complete. The transaction will not be added to the blockchain. Note that the estimate may be significantly more than the amount of gas actually used by the transaction, for a variety of reasons including EVM mechanics and node performance. 

 See `eth_call` parameters, expect that all properties are optional. If no gas limit is specified geth uses the block gas limit from the pending block as an upper bound. As a result the returned estimate might not be enough to executed the call/transaction when the amount of gas is higher than the pending block gas limit.
methods.summary: Calculates an estimate of how much gas is necessary to allow the transaction to complete

methods.name: eth_newFilter
methods.summary: Creates a filter object, based on filter options, to notify when the state changes (logs).
methods.description:
To check if the state has changed, call `eth_getFilterChanges`.

**A note on specifying topic filters**:
Topics are order-dependent. A transaction with a log with topics `[A, B]` will be matched by the following topic filters:

`[]` anything
`[A]` A in first position (and anything after)
`[null, B]` anything in first position AND B in second position (and anything after)
`[A, B]` A in first position AND B in second position (and anything after)
`[[A, B], [A, B]]` (A OR B) in first position AND (A OR B) in second position (and anything after)

result.name: filterId
result.description: The filter ID for use in `eth_getFilterChanges`

methods.name: eth_sign
methods.summary: Calculates an Ethereum specific signature
methods.description:
The sign method calculates an Ethereum specific signature with: `sign(keccak256("\x19Ethereum Signed Message:\n" + len(message) + message)))`.

By adding a prefix to the message makes the calculated signature recognisable as an Ethereum specific signature. This prevents misuse where a malicious DApp can sign arbitrary data (e.g. transaction) and use the signature to impersonate the victim.

**Note** the address to sign with must be unlocked.

result.name: signedMessage
result.description: The signed message

methods.name: txpool_content
methods.summary: Returns the transactions currently in the pool, in full.
methods.description:
Returns two maps, `pending` and `queued`, keyed by sender address and then by decimal nonce. `pending` holds transactions eligible for the next block; `queued` holds those whose nonce leaves a gap and which therefore cannot be executed yet.

The sender address appears twice in every entry, formatted two different ways: bare hex as the map key, and `0x`-prefixed as the transaction's `from`. Both name the same account. Key off the prefixed form or normalise the key before comparing.

result.name: content
result.description: The pending and queued transactions, in full

examples.name: contentExample
examples.description: One ordinary transfer and one contract creation from the same sender. The creation carries `0x00` in `to`, which is how an empty receive address is rendered here.

methods.name: txpool_inspect
methods.summary: Returns a summary of the transactions currently in the pool.
methods.description:
The same `pending` and `queued` grouping as `txpool_content`, but each transaction is reduced to a single `recipient: value wei + gas x gasPrice gas` string, so the pool can be inspected without transferring it in full.

Both addresses here are bare hex without the `0x` prefix: the sender as the map key, and the recipient at the head of the summary string. The value and the gas price are decimal wei, not hex. A transaction that creates a contract has no recipient, so its summary begins with the empty string and a colon.

result.name: inspect
result.description: The pending and queued transactions, one summary string each

examples.name: inspectExample
examples.description: The same two transactions as the `txpool_content` example. The contract creation has no recipient, so its summary begins with a bare colon.

methods.name: txpool_status
methods.summary: Returns how many transactions the pool is holding.
methods.description: Returns the number of transactions eligible for the next block (`pending`) and the number held back because their nonce leaves a gap (`queued`). Both are plain integers, not hex quantities.

result.name: status
result.description: The pending and queued transaction counts

BlockNumberOrTag.title: blockNumberOrTag
BlockNumberOrTag.description:
A block, given as its height in hex or as a tag. A height in decimal is rejected: the block is looked up by `Web3InformationRetriever`, which parses the number as hex and requires the `0x` prefix.

A 32-byte block hash is also accepted in this position and resolves to that block. It is deliberately left out of the union above: the node does not distinguish a hash-length hex string from a height, so the capability is a side effect of how the identifier is parsed rather than a designed one, and publishing it would make it breaking to narrow. Look a block up by hash through the block reference object instead.

BloomFilter.title: bloomFilter
BloomFilter.description: A 2048 bit bloom filter from the logs of the transaction. Each log sets 3 bits though taking the low-order 11 bits of each of the first three pairs of bytes in a Keccak 256 hash of the log's byte series

PoolDestinationAddress.title: poolTo
PoolDestinationAddress.description: Destination address of the transaction, or `0x00` when the transaction creates a contract. A creation transaction carries an empty receive address, and the pool renders empty bytes as the sentinel `0x00` rather than as null. This is specific to the pool: `eth_getTransactionByHash` reports the same transaction's `to` as null.

oneOf.title: contractCreationSentinel
oneOf.description: The transaction creates a contract and has no destination address

ExecutionBlockNumberOrTag.title: executionBlockNumberOrTag
ExecutionBlockNumberOrTag.description: A block to execute against, given as its height in hex or in decimal, or as a tag. The decimal form is accepted because the block is resolved by `ExecutionBlockRetriever`, which parses both bases; the block-reading methods resolve through `Web3InformationRetriever`, which parses hex only and answers `invalid blocknumber` for a decimal height. It is not the only place decimal is taken -- `eth_getBlocksByNumber` parses its own height and accepts both bases too -- but among the methods that take a block parameter it is what separates executing from reading.

RequireCanonical.title: requireCanonical
RequireCanonical.description: Whether a block that is not on the canonical chain is acceptable. Send it as the JSON string `"true"` or `"false"`, not as a JSON boolean: the node reads the whole object as a map of strings, so a non-string value fails during deserialisation, before this field is inspected. A string other than those two is rejected with `Invalid input: requireCanonical must be a String "true" or "false"`. It is only consulted alongside `blockHash`; when it is `"true"` and the referenced block is not on the canonical chain, the node answers with a block-not-found error stating the block is not canonical.

BlockRef.title: blockRef
BlockRef.description: Object defining block references, for a method that reads the block. At least one of `blockHash` or `blockNumber` must be present; the node rejects an object carrying neither with `Invalid block input`. `blockNumber` is hex only here -- a decimal height is answered with `invalid blocknumber`. The method that executes against the block rather than reading it takes `executionBlockRef`, which also accepts decimal.

ExecutionBlockRef.title: executionBlockRef
ExecutionBlockRef.description: A block reference for a method that executes against the block rather than reading it. It is the same object as `blockRef`, except that `blockNumber` may be given in decimal as well as in hex: the height is resolved by `ExecutionBlockRetriever`, which parses both bases, where the reading methods go through `Web3InformationRetriever` and take hex only. At least one of `blockHash` or `blockNumber` must be present; the node rejects an object carrying neither with `Invalid block input`.
